faq.a: Aadam is the Arabic-script form آدم of Adam, the first human in Islamic tradition.

faq.q: Is Aadam the same name as Adam?
faq.a: Yes. Aadam is a transliteration variant for the Arabic form آدم; Adam is the familiar English spelling.

faq.q: Is Aadam mentioned in the Qur’an?
faq.a: Yes. Adam is named in the Qur’an and appears in its account of humanity’s beginnings.

faq.q: Was Adam a prophet in Islam?
faq.a: Yes. Islamic tradition recognises Adam as the first human and a prophet.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aadam?
faq.a: Aadam is the Arabic form of a wider Semitic personal name. This entry avoids claiming one settled deeper etymology.

faq.q: How is Aadam written in Arabic?

faq.a: A practical English approximation is “AA-dam”; pronunciation varies across Arabic, Urdu and English.
It is traditionally used as a masculine given name, reflecting the male figure Adam.
